title: Quant onboarding pilot — retro and action log (Nov 2026)
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures the retrospective notes and concrete action items from the 2-week pilot where we onboarded the new community LLaMA-3-small-compat model variant into the model-onboarding flow with mixed-bit per-layer quantization profiles. Goal: validate correctness/regression characteristics on our small production prompt suite, measure token-level latency and throughput with KV caching enabled, and exercise the rollout/fallback logic in Canary.

Participants (meeting 2026-11-22): Priya (owner), Ethan (infra experiments), Liu (evals), Ava (serving/runtime), Marco (SRE). Quick async notes from others included.

Pilot summary (what we ran):
- Model: llm-v3-small-compat (FP16 baseline) + q4_0 and q3_mixed per-layer profiles (prototype binary from quant-tools PR#45).
- Serving config: dedicated small pool (2x A10g equiv), batch_target=256ms, kv_cache=prefix-only, dynamic_batching enabled.
- Eval set: "prod-mini-100" (200 unique prompts drawn from production traffic, balanced across chat/generation/rewrites).
- Metrics collected: token-level throughput (tokens/s), p95 latency (ms), EM-ish exact-match where applicable, top-level QA pass rates, and embedding drift (cosine) for embed tasks.

Key results (aggregate across the 200 prompt eval):
- Correctness: FP16 baseline EM-like pass = 80.1%. q4_0 = 78.4% (-1.7pp). q3_mixed (selective 3-bit on dense->attn tail) = 76.9% (-3.2pp). Noted degradation concentrated in long-context knowledge-recall prompts.
- Embedding drift: avg cosine drop vs FP16 = 0.008 for q4_0, 0.027 for q3_mixed (acceptable for most similarity workflows, flagged for search rerank use-cases).
- Latency/throughput (with prefix KV cache warm; numbers are median across calls):
  - FP16: throughput 1,180 tok/s; p95 latency 118ms
  - q4_0: throughput 1,640 tok/s; p95 latency 86ms
  - q3_mixed: throughput 1,980 tok/s; p95 latency 72ms
- Memory: VRAM per replica dropped ~21% for q4_0 and ~36% for q3_mixed relative to FP16, enabling higher per-GPU concurrency.

What surprised us:
- Failure modes concentrated on prompts with long exact-recall targets ( > 1,500 token context )—we suspected KV cache interplay, but experiments with disabling prefix cache did not fully restore FP16 EM on q3_mixed.
- q3_mixed improved throughput more than expected without catastrophic correctness loss; many short-chat flows looked identical to FP16 in manual review.
- Small but consistent embedding drift on a subset of legal-doc prompts — needs targeted eval.

Decisions / temporary rollouts we made during pilot:
- Canary: we rolled q4_0 to 10% of internal traffic for a day (night-hours) with auto-fallback to FP16 on increased latency/error. No incidents; minor increase in token-level anomalies observed and tracked in JIRA-ML-987.
- q3_mixed kept as experimental-only behind feature flag; decided NOT to promote to Canary until we resolve long-context regressions.

Open questions / hypotheses to test next sprint:
1) Is the long-context EM drop a quantization artifact or an inference runtime ordering issue (KV index alignment)? Hypothesis: per-layer rounding for attention projection layers accumulates error. Plan: run per-layer ablation where attention proj layers stay q4_0 and others at q3.
2) Does prefix-KV caching amplify small generation errors? Hypothesis: cached KV entries quantized differently cause drift when appended to newer tokens. Plan: run warm-cache vs cold-cache split and simulate repeated prefix reuse across 50k tokens.
3) Is embedding drift reversible with small de-quantization postprocessing (e.g., recovering higher precision for final embed layer)? Quick experiment planned.

Action items (owners, ETA):
- Per-layer ablation jobs (Liu + Ethan) — run targeted ablations on attention proj layers + report by 2026-11-29. (JIRA-ML-987 subtask created).
- KV cache simulation harness (Ethan) — implement replay harness to compare warm vs cold cache scenarios at scale; end-to-end metrics and traces by 2026-11-30.
- Small manual eval set for legal-doc embeddings (Ava) — collect 150 examples, run embedding drift threshold tests, decide accept/reject criteria by 2026-12-02.
- Rollout policy doc update (Priya) — add quant-specific gate: per-prompt-class rollback thresholds and embedding drift soft-fail. Draft by 2026-11-26.
- Instrumentation: add token-level delta traces for cached vs non-cached tokens (Marco + infra) — prototype by 2026-12-06.

Notes to self / team reminders (informal):
- Keep the q3_mixed changes behind feature flag; do not enable on customer-facing default pools until we have per-layer ablation results.
- Ask legal/product for a short list of "safety-critical prompts" where even small correctness regressions are unacceptable. This will help set hard thresholds.

Short-term checklist for next week:
- [ ] Liu: per-layer ablation runs queued and started (target 48h runs).
- [ ] Ethan: KV replay harness skeleton + preliminary replay of 10k prefixes.
- [ ] Ava: manual review of 40 flagged failures, document exact failure patterns.
- [ ] Priya: rollout doc PR opened and link added to Confluence.
- [ ] Marco: sampling-enabled token-delta traces in Canary for q4_0 (low overhead sample).

Links and artifacts: see linked_artifacts above. Also internal note: refer to quant-tools PR#45 for exact quantization config snippets used in pilot (per-layer mapping lives in quant_profiles/llm-v3-small-compat.json in the PR).

Retro takeaways (one-liners):
- Trade-off looks promising: 25–40% throughput gains for 1–3% correctness loss on many workloads; careful per-prompt gating required.
- KV cache interactions are the highest priority unknown — resolving that will unlock safe promotion paths.
- Need targeted eval suites (legal, long-context recall, embeddings) before production promotion.

End of note. If you have additional flagged prompts to add to "prod-mini-100" please drop into the Slack thread linked above or add to JIRA-ML-987 as comments.
